chapter: Union, New Orleans and King Oliver
title: Blue Mondays in 1948 and King Oliver's decline
summary: Reason recalls hosting Oliver's wife and the later health decline of Oliver, who told him he was the last New Orleans musician he would send for.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: And, um, but, uh, um, when I saw Stella, she used to come to my house. With this drummer, um, they used to, they used to take around quite often to see the town and, uh, they used to come to my house. I was living on Liberty, uh, uh, Irana and Liberty. My people used to own that corner. And we used to have something called Blue Monday at my house. And we used to pay the money. The musicians used to come down and, uh, my wife would cook. And we'd play music all day. We used to make our cow, you know, put in, buy liquor and food and everything. And, uh, uh, she'd come up sometime. I can't remember that drummer's name, but I understand that he passed. Now Estella's still living, as you know.
No, she's passed. She passed too, yeah.
But she would be pretty old now.
When was this that you were at Irana?

Right after I came out of the Army. I went back to Detroit. Then I came back to New Orleans in 1948. The latter part of 48. And, uh, uh, uh, uh, with, uh, with Joe, it, it, it, it just seem as if he, as if he had just said, well, just let it all go. Mm-hmm. And, uh, it wasn't good for his business. Wasn't good for his business. And, uh, he was having trouble with his stomach. And that was because of, uh, he had bad teeth. Mm-hmm. And Louis gave him the money three times to have his teeth fixed. The king would not have his teeth fixed. And, um, I don't know whether he was afraid of the doctors or afraid if he had his teeth pulled, he wouldn't be able to play no more or something. Then he, when he took down real ill after that last trip, when I left him in, in, um, Vicksburg, Mississippi, he went back. Yeah, that was Vicksburg, Vicksburg, Mississippi. And he went back to Savannah, Georgia. And someone told me, I didn't see it, but they said that he was, he had either opened a little shop or, a shoeshine shop or something. But his health had gone real bad on him then. And, uh, when he went back that time, that's the last contact that I had. Because when I left, I had been talking to him about three or four weeks that I wasn't happy with what he had there. And, um, I was, if there had been things that had been improved, I was going back to New Orleans. So he told me, he said, well, you will be the last of the New Orleans musicians I'll ever send for. That's what he told me. And he said, uh, it just seemed like you can never get things straightened out like it was years ago. But he was a great musician, but he was slow about business.
